memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near. A star will come out of Jacob; a sceptre will rise out of Israel. He will crush the foreheads of Moab, the skulls of all the people of Sheth." - Num 24:17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here Balaam speaks one of the great prophecies of the Old Testament. He sees a figure who is "not now" and "not near," someone far off in the future. A star will come out of Jacob, a sceptre will rise out of Israel. A star signals something glorious and heaven-sent; a sceptre signals a king who will rule.

For centuries God's people held onto this promise of a coming ruler from Israel. It pointed forward to a King who would triumph over every enemy of God. And Scripture shows us clearly who this King is: the Lord Jesus Christ, the promised One who came from the line of Jacob to reign forever.

We can say with confidence that this prophecy has been fulfilled in Christ. He is the bright Morning Star (Rev 22:16), the King whose sceptre is a sceptre of justice (Heb 1:8). What Balaam glimpsed dimly from afar, we now see clearly in the coming of Jesus. The star has risen; the King has come.

How wonderful that even through a reluctant prophet, God announced the coming of the Saviour long before His birth. The whole of Scripture points to Christ, and here in the wilderness His coming was foretold. Lift your eyes to the Star out of Jacob, the King who has come and who reigns. He is the fulfilment of every ancient hope.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does it strengthen your faith that Christ's coming was foretold so long before?
2. What does it mean to you that Jesus is the King who has come?
3. How can you lift your eyes today to the Star out of Jacob?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You are the Star out of Jacob, the promised King foretold long ago. Thank You for coming as our Saviour and reigning forever. Help me to fix my eyes on You. Amen.
